output.reason: On its own, the cited bullet "container" [ev-ba4422942cd3] says nothing, but the section around it explains it. It is one entry in the ordered list of labels that Loki 3.0 checks to build the `service_name` label [ev-b07a4021f30c]. In that order it comes after service_name, service, app, application, name and app_kubernetes_io_name [ev-92063a2a5bac, ev-2690c7915f58, ev-61d6d2b50a95, ev-c8bbef5b1d06, ev-d0c9247a44d4, ev-33c9df8cd833], and before container_name, component, workload and job [ev-6c97458131e0, ev-73d501ad9fa3, ev-7e86af7082a3, ev-ea984d665a12]. That gives an engineer the subject (the default `discover_service_name` list in limits_config), the change (Loki now adds `service_name` to ingested logs by default, falling back to `unknown_service`), who is exposed (logs without a `service_name` label, unless the list is changed or set empty), and the consequence (an extra `service_name` label is added, with its value taken from `container` when no earlier label in the list matches). This item is one entry of that single `service_name` change, not a separate change of its own.
